text:
Ryan Hartman is having a rough start on a Minnesota team that's having a great one. He has four points in 19 games, one goal on 2.5 expected (the quality of his chances), and the Wild have only 39% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, 19 points worse than without him. That's the weakest relative mark on the team.

That's out of character. Evolving-Hockey had his team creating more with him on the ice last season (89th percentile among forwards), and he drew more penalties than he took. This fall he's been on the other side of that too: two minors in one scrum against Tampa Bay, as Heather Rule noted.

He's 32, with 499 games in Minnesota, and he scored 23 goals last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 57% of his entries. At 13 minutes a night, the Wild aren't relying on him, which is the good news for them. Our projection sees about 14 goals, a big step down unless the chance share turns around.
